headlines.article_text: Alphabet (GOOGL) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Alphabet's third-quarter earnings report lands following a recent slide in the company's stock price. Concerns are mounting across the AI infrastructure space that revenue won't justify the costs. Google's cloud business has been a standout performer in recent quarters and is expected to show revenue growth of 90% from a year earlier, according to LSEG. In this article GOOGL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai speaks at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, India, on Feb. 20, 2026. Prakash Singh | Bloomberg | Getty Images Alphabet is set to report third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Here's what analysts expect, according to a consensus of estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.02 Revenue: $128.2 billion Revenue is expected to increase 25% from a year earlier, which would mark the fastest rate of growth for any period since 2021. Still, the report arrives at a skittish moment on Wall Street, with investors growing more concerned about the costs tied to the artificial intelligence buildout. Shares of the Google parent have dropped in five of the past six sessions through Tuesday and are down about 7% in October. In July, the company lifted its full-year forecast for capital expenditures to between $195 billion and $205 billion, up from prior guidance of as much as $190 billion. At the same time, the company reported negative free cash flow for the first time. For the third quarter, analysts are expecting Alphabet to show capex growth of 130% from a year earlier to $55.2 billion, according to FactSet. Annual capex is expected to top $200 billion before exceeding $300 billion in 2027. Meanwhile, analysts see negative free cash flow of $2.27 billion in the third quarter, and expect that gulf to widen for each of the next four quarters. As Google continues to open its wallet to fuel expansion, it's getting rewarded with revenue growth in its cloud division, home to its AI offerings. The company is projected to show cloud growth of 90% to $28.7 billion, as Google continues taking market share from larger rivals Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure. Microsoft also reports earnings on Wednesday, followed by Amazon on Thursday. Google is aggressively adding its Gemini models and services to its enterprise offerings, and is also ramping up sales of its custom tensor processing units (TPUs), which compete with Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs). At the same time, Google's core business is under pressure from OpenAI and Anthropic as well as from a blitz of new agents on the market. "Google continues to be well-positioned across AI," analysts at Citizens – who recommend buying the stock – wrote in a report last week. "That said, execution risk exists, and we are incrementally cautious on Search as we believe competition is increasing with agents and requires another pivot." Company executives are scheduled to hold a conference call with analysts at 4:30 p.m. ET. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: WEN, WING, FFIV, ENPH, LH Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Wendy's — The fast-food chain climbed 15% after Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management proposed taking Wendy's private for $1.4 billion, according to a regulatory filing . The burger chain has posted same-store sales declines for six consecutive quarters. Brinker International — The owner of Chili's raised its full-year guidance, calling for adjusted earnings of $13.30 to $13.90 per share, beating a FactSet consensus estimate for $13.28. The company also lifted its projections for revenue. Shares were last trading 15% higher. Wingstop — The chicken wing chain jumped 15% after third-quarter earnings topped estimates. Wingstop earned $1.08 per share, excluding certain items, while analysts polled by LSEG sought $1.02 per share. Revenue, however, fell short at $185 million compared to the consensus estimate of $193 million. F5 — The cybersecurity company tanked about 19%. F5's guidance for fiscal year 2027 calls for non-GAAP earnings of $18 to $18.30 per share, while the FactSet consensus estimate sought $18.03 per share. Piper Sandler also downgraded shares to neutral from overweight. Labcorp — The lab diagnostics company advanced 10% on the back of a guidance raise for the full year. Labcorp sees adjusted earnings in a range of $18.30 to $18.70 per share on revenue of $14.779 billion to $14.887 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $18.35 per share on $14.75 billion. GE HealthCare Technologies — Shares gained 8% after GE HealthCare Technologies lifted its full-year guidance. The company anticipates adjusted earnings will range from $4.95 to $5.05 per share, and it sees organic revenue growth of roughly 4% year over year. CoStar — The commercial real estate data company lost 13% after full-year revenue guidance largely failed to impress the Street. CoStar sees revenue in a range of $3.75 billion to $3.77 billion, roughly in line with the FactSet consensus estimate for $3.75 billion. Ultralife — Shares surged 145% after EnerSys agreed to acquire the battery manufacturer for $16 per share in cash. The transaction values Ultralife at approximately $320 million. The New York-based technology company announced the merger agreement after the market closed on Tuesday. EnerSys shares gained 2%. Enphase Energy — The solar stock tumbled 16% after quarterly revenue declined to $293.3 million from $410.4 million a year earlier. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance also missed the mark, ranging from $225 million to $255 million, versus the FactSet consensus estimate for $297.6 million. PPG Industries — Shares were up almost 6% after PPG reported quarterly earnings of $2.25 per share on an adjusted basis, beating the FactSet consensus estimate of $2.12 per share. The coatings manufacturer also raised the midpoint of its full-year earnings guidance. Robinhood — Shares fell 2% after the brokerage's quarterly profit missed expectations , landing at 51 cents a share and missing the LSEG consensus estimate for 56 cents per share. Revenue increased 12% to $1.42 billion, but cryptocurrency revenue dropped 55% to $120 million. SK hynix — The chipmaker advanced 11% after third-quarter operating profit beat the StreetAccount consensus estimate , fueled by demand for artificial intelligence memory products. The company also announced a special dividend tied to gains from its Kioxia investment. Logitech — The computer peripherals maker dropped more than 11% after the company reported mixed results for the fiscal second quarter. While Logitech's adjusted earnings per share of $1.51 beat a FactSet consensus of $1.30, operating income came in below expectations. Vertiv — The critical digital infrastructure stock rallied 14% after Vertiv topped expectations in its third-quarter report and issued stronger-than-expected guidance for the current quarter and full year. Adjusted earnings of $2.21 per share topped the $1.82 expected by analysts polled by FactSet. Revenue of $4.31 billion exceeded the consensus estimate of $3.75 billion. GE Vernova — Shares were down 2% after the energy equipment company agreed to acquire high-voltage components manufacturer Trench Group for approximately $9 billion. Separately, the company raised its full-year revenue forecast to a range of $46.5 billion to $47.5 billion. — CNBC's Nick Wells, Sarah Min and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.

Dimitar Dilkoff | AFP | Getty Images Microsoft is set to report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday. The software giant has been working to become a bigger force in artificial intelligence through infrastructure expansion and product enhancements, while continuing to produce free cash flow, unlike its fellow hyperscalers. Cloud rivals Alphabet and Amazon , which report results on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively, both showed negative free cash flow in the June quarter, while Meta said last week that it went free cash flow negative in the third quarter. As of Tuesday's close, Microsoft shares were up almost 10% year to date, trailing the S&P 500 index, which has gained about 13% over the same period. During the fiscal first quarter, Microsoft said it would cut 4,800 jobs , and followed up by announcing on Monday that it's offering buyouts to up to 60,000 employees, as it strives to balance a costly AI build-out with capital efficiency. Analysts surveyed by StreetAccount projected $50.67 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases for the quarter. Microsoft also established, during the quarter, an AI implementation unit and revealed a Copilot AI "super app " with coding abilities. Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty Images DETROIT — Ford Motor is set to announce third-quarter earnings after the markets close Wednesday. Here's what Wall Street expects, based on average analysts' estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 40 cents adjusted, estimated Automotive revenue: $46.24 billion estimated Those results would mark a 2% decline in revenue compared with a year earlier and a roughly 11% decrease in adjusted earnings per share. Ford's 2025 third-quarter results included $47.19 billion in automotive revenue, net income of $2.4 billion and earnings per share of 45 cents adjusted. A main focus for investors will be Ford's F-Series pickup trucks, including its crucial F-150. The automaker has been recovering from supplier issues that affected truck production for much of the past year, but experienced a disruption in F-150 manufacturing due to a separate, unrelated supplier problem toward the end of September. Ford reported production of the F-150 declined from more than 57,500 units in August to less than 43,000 in September. The automaker said the disruption is "containable within" its existing 2026 adjusted earnings guidance. Wall Street analysts generally expect Ford to maintain its 2026 outlook, but they differ on how the F-150 production disruption will ultimately affect the automaker's third-quarter results. They're also watching for any changes or surprises in the company's warranty costs.
